correctness.rationale: For all fixed \(r,\gamma,D_v>0\), stationary regeneration gives a Gaussian position mixture over an exponential reset age. Its exact variance is \(\varepsilon^2 h(t)^2+2D_v\int_0^t h(s)^2ds\). Since \(h(t)=t+O(t^2)\), the short-age variance is \(\varepsilon^2t^2+(2D_v/3)t^3\) to the controlled relative error used in the proof. Under \(t=\varepsilon^2u/c\) and \(x=\varepsilon^3y/c\), rescaled integrands converge with an integrable short-time majorant for nonzero \(y\), while the long-time part is \(O(\varepsilon)\). Small-argument asymptotics follow by splitting at a fixed cutoff and using the exponential integral \(E_1\) and a closed antiderivative; large-argument asymptotics follow a cubic scaling substitution and a \(\Gamma(1/6)\) integral. The positive-variance logarithm and zero-variance power law follow independently from the exact mixture. Prefactors and physical normalization are explicit. The packaged verifier passes 47 finite numerical diagnostics; these are not used to infer infinite limits.

value.rationale: The closest paper identifies a physically important contrast between exact-zero and equilibrated Gaussian velocity resetting. It is natural to ask how arbitrarily weak residual velocity thermalization changes the local stationary spatial density. The theorem supplies an explicit interpolating profile and sharp rescalings \(\varepsilon^3/c\) for space and \(r/\varepsilon\) for amplitude, including both asymptotic constants. It demonstrates a noncommuting singular perturbation rather than merely reproducing known endpoints or calculating an arbitrary parameter slice.
